annotation_description: Playing Soulstone Sanctuary on turn 1 instead of a colored mana source is suboptimal. The hand contains two 1-drop creatures (Burnout Bashtronaut and Hired Claw) that require red mana to cast. Soulstone Sanctuary only produces colorless mana (its creature activation costs 4 generic), so playing it turn 1 means no creature can be deployed this turn. Playing Mountain or Rockface Village would allow casting Burnout Bashtronaut or Hired Claw immediately, developing the board and starting to pressure the opponent. Rockface Village is arguably the best choice since it can produce red for creatures and has the pump activation for Lizards (relevant with two Hired Claws in hand).

During the opponent's end step (combat phase end on their turn 1), Gem3P Stoic declined to cast Opt, which is a pure-upside instant that could be cast at end of opponent's turn with no downside. Casting Opt here would use the available mana (Spirebluff Canal produces U or R) to scry 1 and draw a card, improving card selection and hand quality at no cost since the mana would otherwise go unused. There's no reason to hold the mana open — Spell Snare can't counter anything meaningful on turn 1 with the opponent having only 1 mana, and there are no other productive uses for the mana.

Gem3P Stoic passed the turn with mana available and Opt in hand. Opt is an instant that cantrips (scry 1, draw a card) with pure upside. There's no reason not to cast it at end of opponent's turn to dig deeper into the deck and improve card quality. Passing without using available mana on a cantrip wastes tempo. While Opt could technically be cast on the opponent's end step, the decision here was to pass entirely without casting it, and the game log shows the turn moved to the opponent without Opt being cast.

Playing Mountain instead of Rockface Village is slightly suboptimal. The hand contains two Hired Claws (Lizards), and Rockface Village can both produce red mana for creatures and later activate its ability to give a Lizard +1/+0 and haste. Since the deck is creature-heavy with Lizards, Rockface Village provides strictly more utility than a basic Mountain in this context. The creature mana restriction on Rockface Village's red production is largely irrelevant here since most of the hand is creatures anyway.

Playing a creature in the precombat main phase when holding combat tricks or pump abilities and facing an opponent with open blue mana (Spirebluff Canal) is generally suboptimal. More importantly, Burnout Bashtronaut with menace is arguably the better turn 2 play here - it has menace making it harder to block, and its speed mechanic rewards early aggression. Since the opponent has only one land and likely can't block effectively anyway, the menace creature that grows with the speed mechanic and can eventually gain double strike is a stronger aggressive play than a 1/2 that needs other Lizards to trigger its ping ability. Additionally, casting a creature before playing the Rockface Village land drop is a sequencing error - playing Rockface Village first would give the option to use its haste-granting ability on a Lizard creature, though in this case the creature is being cast with the Mountain mana so it doesn't affect available mana this turn.

Gem3P Stoic declined to cast Opt at the end of their opponent's turn or during their own precombat main phase. With Spirebluff Canal untapped providing blue mana, casting Opt would scry 1 and draw a card for just {U}, helping find a second land drop (they have Multiversal Passage and Spirebluff Canal in hand but need to develop). While holding up Spell Snare is reasonable, the opponent's lands are both tapped, so there's no threat coming this turn cycle. Casting Opt now helps dig toward lands and action. That said, they could also be planning to play a land and hold up Spell Snare on the opponent's turn 2 play — but the opponent already took their turn 2 (it's now Gem3P's turn 2), so holding Spell Snare mana is for the opponent's turn 3. They could cast Opt now, play Spirebluff Canal (their second land from hand), and still have Spell Snare mana up. Actually, looking more carefully: they have one Spirebluff Canal on the battlefield. They could play Multiversal Passage as their land for turn, cast Opt with Spirebluff Canal, and still have Multiversal Passage untapped — but Passage only adds one color based on choice. They could choose Island and have UU open for two Spell Snares, or cast Opt and have one Spell Snare up. Given the opponent has Hired Claw (a 1/2 that can grow), holding Spell Snare for a 2-mana spell is reasonable, but casting Opt to find lands/answers while still having Spell Snare available after playing their land seems strictly better than doing nothing.

During the opponent's combat step (or end of turn), Gem3P Stoic has open mana on Spirebluff Canal and could cast Opt to draw a card and scry 1 at instant speed, using mana that would otherwise go unused. This is a pure-value play at end of opponent's turn that costs nothing strategically - they have no reason to hold up the single blue mana since they're not in a position to cast Spell Snare (which counters MV 2 spells, and opponent's lands are tapped). Declining to Opt here wastes mana and misses a free card draw opportunity.

With the opponent tapped out and no pressure requiring interaction, this is the ideal time to cast Opt at end of turn or during the main phase to dig through the deck. While passing priority here isn't terrible (they could cast Opt on opponent's end step), they should at minimum cast Opt now or plan to cast it on the opponent's end step. However, the bigger missed opportunity is that Burst Lightning on Hired Claw while the opponent is tapped out would be clean removal of a threat that grows with +1/+1 counters and pings when Lizards attack. Removing it now prevents it from accumulating value, and the opponent can't protect it.

Gem3P Stoic has 2 untapped lands and could cast Opt at instant speed during the opponent's end step, but more importantly, they're passing their main phase without casting anything when they have useful options. Casting Opt now to dig for a land drop (they need to develop their mana for Eddymurk Crab) would be reasonable, but the real issue is that they should hold up Spell Snare with their two mana since the opponent has a 2-mana-value creature already deployed and might cast another 2-cost spell. However, they could cast Opt at end of opponent's turn instead to hold up Spell Snare, which makes passing here defensible. The pass is actually reasonable if they plan to hold up Spell Snare and cast Opt at end of turn.

Gem3P Stoic declined to cast Opt at the end of the opponent's combat step (or during combat), which is a missed opportunity. Opt is a pure card-selection spell that should be cast at end of opponent's turn to use mana efficiently. With two untapped Spirebluff Canals and holding Opt plus two Spell Snares, they could cast Opt now during opponent's turn while still holding up Spell Snare (costs U). Since opponent already tapped out (Mountain and Soulstone Sanctuary are tapped), there's nothing to counter this turn, so using one mana for Opt loses nothing. Even if they want to hold up both Spell Snares, they have two lands and Opt + Spell Snare each cost U, so they could cast both. Declining Opt here means they'll likely want to cast it on their own turn, which is worse timing since it could interfere with their development.

Gem3P Stoic passed the turn with 2 mana open and useful instant-speed spells in hand. Opt is a pure-upside cantrip that could be cast at end of opponent's turn to dig for lands or answers while using mana that would otherwise go to waste. With 7 cards in hand including Eddymurk Crab (which gets cheaper with instants/sorceries in the graveyard), casting Opt on the opponent's end step would both use available mana and fuel the Crab discount. They also need to hit land drops to cast their spells. While holding up Spell Snare has some value, the opponent already has 2 lands and is likely to deploy 1-mana or 3+ mana threats, making Spell Snare less critical this turn.

Burnout Bashtronaut does NOT have haste - the player's reasoning incorrectly assumes it does. It's a 1/1 menace creature that cannot attack this turn. The player should have cast Tersa Lightshatter instead, which actually has haste and is a 3/3 that can attack immediately. With 3 lands available (Mountain, Mountain, Soulstone Sanctuary providing colorless), the player has exactly {2}{R} to cast Tersa. Tersa would provide immediate pressure with a 3/3 haste attacker and a card filtering ETB trigger (discard up to 2, draw that many), which is significantly more impactful than deploying a 1/1 that can't attack yet. Playing Bashtronaut first also means Tersa can't be cast next turn alongside another spell as easily, losing tempo.

Burnout Bashtronaut is a 1-mana creature ({R}), so Spell Snare cannot counter it (CMC 1, not 2). However, the player declined to cast Burst Lightning or Opt in response to the Bashtronaut being on the stack. Burst Lightning could have killed the 1/1 Bashtronaut on the stack (as a counterspell-like effect isn't possible, but after it resolves the player could kill it on their own turn). The player passed priority, letting Bashtronaut resolve. Since the opponent already has Hired Claw, Bashtronaut with menace adds another attacker that triggers Hired Claw's damage ability. With the speed mechanic, Bashtronaut can become very threatening if it reaches max speed (double strike). Casting Burst Lightning now to remove it immediately (after resolution, during main phase response) would prevent it from attacking and gaining speed. However, the player may prefer to hold Burst Lightning for a bigger threat or use it on their own turn. This is debatable but letting a speed-ramping menace creature live when you have efficient removal is at least questionable.

Casting Hired Claw before combat is suboptimal. The opponent has only two Spirebluff Canals (UU or UR open) and could have Spell Snare (counters MV 2 spells) or other interaction. More importantly, casting creatures before combat when you have combat tricks or want to preserve information is generally worse. Here, Burnout Bashtronaut has menace and the opponent has no blockers, so attacking first would deal damage, potentially trigger speed increases, and then post-combat you could cast Hired Claw with full information. Additionally, if the opponent had a way to punish overextension, playing the creature pre-combat gives them more information about your board before you attack. The Rockface Village activation (+1/+0 and haste to a Lizard) is sorcery-speed only, so if the plan was to give the new Hired Claw haste via Rockface Village, that would require tapping Rockface Village and paying R - but all mana sources appear tapped except Rockface Village. Actually, Rockface Village is untapped and could tap for R to cast Hired Claw, then there's no mana left for the activation. So the Hired Claw won't attack this turn anyway. The correct sequence is: attack with Burnout Bashtronaut first (menace, no blockers = free damage, advances speed), then cast Hired Claw post-combat.

Gem3P Stoic declined to cast Burst Lightning in response to Hired Claw being cast. Hired Claw is a 1/2 Lizard that deals 1 damage whenever Lizards attack, and can grow with +1/+1 counters. The opponent already has Burnout Bashtronaut on board, so the Hired Claw's Lizard attack trigger won't fire (Bashtronaut is a Goblin, not a Lizard), but Hired Claw itself is a Lizard and will trigger its own ability when it attacks. However, Burst Lightning costs R and would use one of only two available lands, leaving Gem3P unable to hold up Spell Snare on the opponent's turn. With two Spell Snares in hand and only two lands, preserving the mana for a potential counter next turn is defensible. Still, letting Hired Claw resolve means it can start growing and dealing incremental damage, and Burst Lightning kills it cleanly. The decision to not remove it is debatable since the opponent could play more Lizards or use Hired Claw's pump ability.

Gem3P Stoic passed on casting Opt during their precombat main phase with 2 untapped lands and no other plays worth making this turn. While holding up Spell Snare is reasonable, the opponent's board already has multiple threats deployed (two Hired Claws and a Burnout Bashtronaut), and the opponent's lands are all tapped. Casting Opt now would help dig toward answers (like finding a third land drop or removal) while the opponent can't cast anything meaningful. Additionally, Opt in the graveyard reduces Eddymurk Crab's cost. The player still needs to play a land this turn (Multiversal Passage or Riverpyre Verge), so they could cast Opt, then play their land and still have mana available. However, saving Spell Snare mana for the opponent's turn has some value, making this debatable.

The opponent has no creatures to block. Attacking with only one Hired Claw instead of all eligible creatures leaves free damage on the table. The reasoning incorrectly states only Burnout Bashtronaut can attack due to haste, but the game offered 'All attack' as an option, indicating multiple creatures were eligible.

Targeted the attacking Hired Claw instead of Burnout Bashtronaut. Bashtronaut is a scaling threat with menace that gains double strike at max speed, making it far more dangerous long-term. The 1 combat damage saved by killing the attacker is negligible compared to the escalating threat of Bashtronaut. The other untapped Hired Claw still provides Lizard attack triggers anyway.

Playing Riverpyre Verge before Multiversal Passage means Riverpyre Verge can only produce {R} (not {U}) since there's no Island or Mountain in play. Playing Multiversal Passage first (choosing Island) would make Riverpyre Verge fully functional when played later, and would also provide 3 blue sources immediately.

Casting Sleight of Hand (a sorcery) instead of Opt (an instant) during the main phase is suboptimal for two reasons: (1) Opt could be cast at end of opponent's turn, leaving mana open for Spell Snare during the opponent's turn 3, which is a critical tempo window. By casting Sleight of Hand now, they use their mana proactively and lose the ability to hold up Spell Snare this turn cycle. (2) However, they have two Spell Snares and only one untapped land would remain either way after casting a 1-mana spell and playing Multiversal Passage tapped — actually, they have 3 lands and could play Multiversal Passage as their land drop. If they play Passage (paying 2 life for untapped or letting it enter tapped) they'd have 4 mana sources. But the key issue is: they should save their instant-speed card draw (Opt) for the opponent's end step and cast the sorcery now if they must cast something now. Wait — that's actually what they did. Sleight of Hand is a sorcery so it MUST be cast on their own turn. Opt is an instant that could be saved. So casting Sleight of Hand now and saving Opt for later is actually correct sequencing. Let me reconsider... The question is whether they should cast anything at all right now or hold up Spell Snare mana. They have 3 lands and haven't played a land yet. If they play Multiversal Passage untapped (paying 2 life), they'd have 4 lands, enough to cast Sleight of Hand AND hold up Spell Snare. So the play of Sleight of Hand now is fine if they also play the land. Actually, looking more carefully, the decision is specifically between Sleight of Hand and Opt — both cost {U}. Casting the sorcery now and saving the instant for later is correct. This isn't a blunder.

Gem3P Stoic chose Winternight Stories over Island from Sleight of Hand. They already have 3 lands in play and Multiversal Passage in hand (which can come in untapped for 2 life), so they'll have 4 mana next turn. However, they need to hit land drops to eventually cast Eddymurk Crab (7 mana, reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard - currently 2 in graveyard so it costs 5). Taking Island would ensure a smooth 4th land drop without paying life for Multiversal Passage, and would enable holding up both Spell Snares more comfortably. Winternight Stories is a powerful draw spell but costs 3 mana and requires discarding, and the player already has a decent hand with reactive spells. The choice is defensible since Winternight Stories provides card advantage and fills the graveyard to reduce Eddymurk Crab's cost, but taking the Island to guarantee the land drop and preserve life total against an aggressive opponent with menace and haste creatures could have been better.

Failed to play a land before casting Tersa Lightshatter. Both Mountain and Rockface Village were available as land drops. Playing a land first is strictly better sequencing — it doesn't change what can be cast but ensures the land drop isn't forgotten, and Rockface Village specifically provides utility to pump Hired Claw (a Lizard). The player's reasoning incorrectly stated they couldn't play a land.

Discarding Nova Hellkite instead of Rockface Village as part of Tersa Lightshatter's ETB discard-then-draw effect. Nova Hellkite is a powerful 4/5 flying haste finisher that can also be warped for 2R. While keeping a land drop is reasonable to avoid mana issues, the player already has 3 lands in play and Tersa is drawing replacement cards. Nova Hellkite represents a much higher power level card than a utility land, and with an aggressive board of Bashtronaut, Hired Claw, and Tersa already applying pressure, having a 5-drop finisher (or a 3-mana warp option) could be more valuable than a 4th land that only adds colorless/red creature mana.

Casting Winternight Stories (3 mana sorcery) on turn 4 taps out the player, leaving no mana to hold up the two Spell Snares in hand. The opponent has Hired Claw in the graveyard and could cast 2-mana threats. Additionally, at 12 life facing an aggressive board (Burnout Bashtronaut, Hired Claw, Tersa Lightshatter all attacking), spending the entire turn drawing cards rather than holding up interaction is risky. Casting Opt at end of opponent's turn would leave up Spell Snare mana and still dig for answers, though Winternight Stories does draw more cards. The opponent's creatures are all tapped, so there's some safety, but the player also needs to find answers quickly and Winternight Stories requires discarding 2 cards (unless discarding a creature), which could be costly.
